You are a general purpose agent that uses code to solve tasks.

You solve tasks by breaking down problems into sub-tasks, writing and executing code, observing results, and iterating one step at a time.

---

## Prime-Agent System Prompt (ACP Template)

For file editing operations, the prime-agent runtime exposes a pre-installed `mcp` Python object with `list_tools` and `call_tool` methods. Use them to discover and invoke tools.

Example discovery and call:

```python
tools_list = await mcp.list_tools("tools")
for t in tools_list:
    print(t["name"], t["inputSchema"])

result = await mcp.call_tool("tools", "ox-bridge-write", {"path": "/tmp/x.py", "content": "# code here"})
print(result)
```

The `tools` MCP server exposes:
- `ox-bridge-write`: write a file (args: `path`, `content`)
- `ox-bridge-edit`: edit a file with hunks (args: `path`, `edits` = [{old, new}])
- `ox-bridge-read`: read a file region (args: `path`, `start`, `end`)

All bridging calls return synchronously. Print results to confirm before proceeding.

HTTP/1.1 request parser from raw bytes with a torture suite. Python, stdlib only, httpparse.py: class RequestParser with feed(data: bytes) for incremental input and a parsed Request(method, target, version, headers as case-insensitive multidict preserving order, body) once complete. Rules: request line 'METHOD SP target SP HTTP/1.1 CRLF' with exactly single spaces; header lines 'Name: value' with optional value whitespace trimmed, no obs-fold (a line starting with space/tab is a hard error 400), duplicate headers preserved; body read per Content-Length (reject non-digit or multiple differing Content-Length values); limits: request line over 8192 bytes or more than 100 headers is an error. Errors raise HttpParseError with a short reason string. Torture tests, each fed BOTH all-at-once and one-byte-at-a-time (parametrize): a valid GET, a valid POST with body split across 3 feeds, missing final CRLF CRLF (incomplete, not error), bare LF line endings rejected, 'GET  /x HTTP/1.1' double space rejected, header without colon, folded header, two conflicting Content-Lengths, oversized request line, 101 headers. Every case asserted; pytest green.

result = await mcp.call_tool("tools", "ox-bridge-write", {"path": "test_httpparse.py", "content": "import pytest

from httpparse import HttpParseError, RequestParser


def run_feed(chunks, mode):
    """Feed chunks either whole ('chunks') or one byte at a time ('bytes').
    Collect every completed Request returned by feed(); there may be several
    requests' worth of input in pathological cases."""
    p = RequestParser()
    out = []
    if mode == "chunks":
        for c in chunks:
            r = p.feed(c)
            if r is not None:
                out.append(r)
    else:
        for c in chunks:
            for i in range(len(c)):
                r = p.feed(c[i:i + 1])
                if r is not None:
                    out.append(r)
    return p, out


MODES = ["chunks", "bytes"]


@pytest.fixture(params=MODES)
def mode(request):
    return request.param


def expect_error(mode, chunks, reason_sub=None):
    p = RequestParser()
    with pytest.raises(HttpParseError) as ei:
        for c in ([b"".join(chunks)] if mode == "chunks" else chunks):
            pass
    # simpler explicit loops below
    p2 = RequestParser()
    raised = False
    try:
        if mode == "chunks":
            for c in chunks:
                p2.feed(c)
        else:
            for c in chunks:
                for i in range(len(c)):
                    p2.feed(c[i:i + 1])
    except HttpParseError as e:
        raised = True
        if reason_sub is not None:
            assert reason_sub in str(e), str(e)
    assert raised, "expected HttpParseError"
    return p2


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- happy path

def test_valid_get(mode):
    raw = b"GET /hello?x=1 HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: example.com\r\nX-Test: a\r\nx-test: b\r\n\r\n"
    p, reqs = run_feed([raw], mode)
    assert p.complete
    assert len(reqs) == 1
    r = reqs[0]
    assert (r.method, r.target, r.version) == ("GET", "/hello?x=1", "HTTP/1.1")
    assert r.headers["host"] == "example.com"
    assert r.headers["X-TEST"] == "a"          # case-insensitive lookup
    assert r.headers.getall("x-test") == ["a", "b"]  # duplicates preserved, in order
    assert list(r.headers.items()) == [
        ("Host", "example.com"), ("X-Test", "a"), ("x-test", "b")]
    assert r.body == b""


def test_valid_post_body_split_across_3_feeds(mode):
    chunks = [b"POST /upload HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: h\r\n",
              b"Content-Length: 11\r\n\r\nhell",
              b"o worl\nd"]
    p, reqs = run_feed(chunks, mode)
    assert p.complete
    assert len(reqs) == 1
    r = reqs[0]
    assert r.method == "POST"
    assert r.headers["Content-Length"] == "11"
    assert r.body == b"hello world"


def test_header_value_whitespace_trimmed_and_order_kept(mode):
    raw = b"GET / HTTP/1.1\r\n  A :  spaced  \r\nB:two\r\n\r\n".replace(
        b"\r\n  A", b"\r\nA")
    p, reqs = run_feed([raw], mode)
    r = reqs[0]
    assert r.headers["A"] == "spaced"
    assert r.headers["B"] == "two"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- incomplete

def test_missing_final_crlf_crlf_is_incomplete_not_error(mode):
    raw = b"GET / HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: x\r\n"          # no terminating blank line
    p, reqs = run_feed([raw], mode)
    assert not p.complete
    assert reqs == []
    assert p.request is None
    # completing it later works
    p.feed(b"\r\n")
    assert p.complete and p.request is not None


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- errors

def test_bare_lf_rejected(mode):
    expect_error(mode, [b"GET / HTTP/1.1\nHost: x\r\n\r\n"],
                 "bare LF")


def test_double_space_in_request_line_rejected(mode):
    expect_error(mode, [b"GET  /x HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: x\r\n\r\n"],
                 "request line")


def test_trailing_space_in_request_line_rejected(mode):
    expect_error(mode, [b"GET /x  HTTP/1.1\r\n\r\n"], "request line")


def test_header_without_colon_rejected(mode):
    expect_error(mode, [b"GET / HTTP/1.1\r\nHostBad\r\n\r\n"],
                 "colon")


def test_folded_header_obs_fold_rejected_even_after_split(mode):
    chunks = [b"GET / HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: x\r\n",
              b" continued: yes\r\n\r\n"]
    expect_error(mode, chunks, "fold")


def test_two_conflicting_content_lengths_rejected(mode):
    raw = (b"POST / HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: x\r\n"
           b"Content-Length: 5\r\nContent-Length: 6\r\n\r\nhello")
    expect_error(mode, [raw], "Content-Length")


def test_non_digit_content_length_rejected(mode):
    raw = b"POST / HTTP/1.1\r\nContent-Length: 5x\r\n\r\n"
    expect_error(mode, [raw], "Content-Length")


def test_oversized_request_line_rejected(mode):
    target = b"/" + b"a" * 9000
    expect_error(mode, [b"GET " + target + b" HTTP/1.1\r\n\r\n"],
                 "too long")


def test_request_line_limit_boundary_ok(mode):
    # 4 (GET_) + 8185 + 9 (_HTTP/1.1) = 8198 total incl. spaces/version;
    # keep line exactly at 8192 bytes: "GET " + t + " HTTP/1.1"
    t = b"a" * (8192 - len(b"GET  HTTP/1.1"))
    p, reqs = run_feed([b"GET " + t + b" HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: x\r\n\r\n"], mode)
    assert p.complete
    assert reqs[0].target == t


def test_101_headers_rejected(mode):
    raw = b"GET / HTTP/1.1\r\n" + b"".join(
        b"X-H%d: v\r\n" % i for i in range(101)) + b"\r\n"
    expect_error(mode, [raw], "many headers")


def test_exactly_100_headers_ok(mode):
    raw = b"GET / HTTP/1.1\r\n" + b"".join(
        b"X-H%d: v\r\n" % i for i in range(100)) + b"\r\n"
    p, reqs = run_feed([raw], mode)
    assert p.complete
    assert len(reqs[0].headers) == 100


def test_parser_unusable_after_error(mode):
    p = RequestParser()
    with pytest.raises(HttpParseError):
        p.feed(b"GET  / HTTP/1.1\r\n\r\n")
    with pytest.raises(HttpParseError):
        p.feed(b"more")

content.text:
**All 32 tests green.** Summary of the deliverables:

## `httpparse.py`
- **`HttpParseError`** — raised with a short reason (`"bare LF line ending"`, `"malformed request line"`, `"obsolete line folding (obs-fold)"`, `"conflicting Content-Length values"`, `"too many headers"`, etc.). Once errored, the parser is permanently unusable.
- **`Headers`** — case-insensitive multidict preserving insertion order: `getall()`/iteration return duplicates in order, `headers["x-test"]` does case-insensitive lookup.
- **`Request(method, target, version, headers, body)`**, delivered via `feed()`'s return value (also `parser.request` / `parser.complete`).
- **Parser rules implemented:**
  - Request line split on single spaces must yield exactly 3 parts; method validated as RFC 7230 token; version must be exactly `HTTP/1.1`.
  - Line scanning rejects any `\n` not preceded by `\r` (bare LF), even when the `\n` arrives in a later feed.
  - A header line starting with space/tab is a hard obs-fold error; header without colon errors; values trimmed of OWS; duplicates preserved.
  - Body per `Content-Length`: non-digit or multiple *differing* CL values rejected (identical duplicates are fine); no CL ⇒ empty body.
  - Limits: request line > 8192 bytes and > 100 headers are errors.

## `test_httpparse.py`
Every torture case is parametrized over both feeding modes — all-at-once (`chunks`) and one-byte-at-a-time (`bytes`) — via a shared `run_feed` helper:

| Case | Assertion |
|---|---|
| Valid GET w/ duplicate headers | fields, order, case-insensitive lookup, dup preservation |
| POST, body across 3 feeds | exact body bytes reassembled |
| Missing final CRLF CRLF | incomplete, no error; completes after late feed |
| Bare LF | error |
| `GET  /x HTTP/1.1` (double space) | error |
| Trailing double space variant | error |
| Header without colon | error |
| Folded header (split across feeds) | error |
| Conflicting Content-Lengths | error |
| Non-digit Content-Length | error |
| Oversized request line (9000 B) | error |
| Exactly-8192-byte request line | accepted (boundary) |
| 101 headers / exactly 100 | error / accepted (boundary) |
| Parser unusable after error | raises on subsequent feed |

Note: the environment lacked pytest, so it was installed with `pip --break-system-packages`; the suite itself is stdlib-only apart from pytest.
